description: TERRAbase maps Earth's most extreme locations to find perfect stand-ins for the Moon and Mars. By analyzing NASA terrain, climate, and soil data, our platform pinpoints optimal terrestrial testing grounds for future planetary missions.
summary: TERRAbase is a web application for planetary science and mission planning, which links Earth-based terrestrial analogues with lunar and Martian analogues through NASA open data. The testing of equipment such as rovers, habitats, and astronaut work flow processes in space is too costly, hence mission planners utilize Earth-based extreme terrains like lava tube, basalt volcanic terrain and hyper-arid deserts, which serve as analogues to off-Earth locations. Through the use of TERRAbase, scientists, students and mission planners have the ability to view a map of discoveries, compare quantitative measures of compatibility (topography, soil mineralogy, thermal delta and radiation shielding), carry out hardware stress simulation in real-time and view planetary analogue specimens in 3D. The linking together of geologic and orbit data in a single dashboard has greatly aided pre-flight hardware validation process.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

TERRAbase (Terrestrial Analogue Explorer) is a full-stack interactive web platform designed to bridge Earth-based field geology with lunar and Martian mission planning. Key modules include:

• Interactive Global Discovery Map: Maps high-priority Earth analogue sites to corresponding Moon and Mars targets with instant site selection.

• Quantitative Compatibility Matrix: Compares Earth and off-world targets across four core engineering parameters—Topography, Soil/Mineral Composition, Thermal Delta, and Radiation Shielding.

• Hardware Stress Tester: Lets users simulate extreme temperature, basaltic regolith, and radiation-shielding conditions on mission payloads (such as the VIPER Lunar Rover Wheel) to evaluate failure vectors and risk levels.

• 3D Spatial Specimen Inspector & Archive Decks: Provides interactive 3D inspection alongside dedicated Lunar and Martian analogue archive decks, plus one-click JSON and NASA text report exports.

Tools, Languages & Development Stack

• Frontend & UI: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, and custom GPU-accelerated CSS/IntersectionObserver animations.

• Deployment & Hosting: Built and deployed via Bolt.new with version control hosted publicly on GitHub (https://github.com/sg150028-bit/TERRAbase) and supplementary archive decks hosted on Framer.

• Data Integration: Synthesized open telemetry and geological parameters from NASA Earthdata, JPL, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (HiRISE), USGS, ESA, and Copernicus.

Impact & Creativity

Instead of static spreadsheets or isolated research papers, TERRAbase turns planetary analogue data into an interactive mission-control simulator. It helps engineers identify terrestrial testbeds before launch while serving as an intuitive educational tool for students exploring comparative planetology.
